charts.title: Calmer-sounding clips are rated less energetic, and also less pleasant.
charts.takeaway: The calm index correlates −0.394 with rated arousal and −0.375 with rated valence, where the forecast was above 0. Both sit far outside the shuffle range of −0.076 to +0.074.
charts.units: partial correlation: the correlation left after loudness, genre and year are held fixed, −1 to 1; below 0 means a higher score goes with a lower rating. Calm index: one score per clip that rises with a longer tail (how long sound rings on after each note) and a darker spectrum (less energy in high frequencies)
charts.n: 502 held-out clips by 270 artists, from 1,744 rated clips
charts.baseline: Calm index shuffled across the test clips 1,000 times: 5th to 95th percentile −0.076 to +0.074 for arousal, −0.078 to +0.077 for valence
charts.threshold: Arousal: below 0, interval below 0, and below the shuffle's 5th percentile. Valence: above 0, interval above 0, and above the shuffle's 95th percentile
charts.ruled_out: A calm index that goes with more pleasant ratings: the valence interval ends at −0.280, and −0.123 with arousal held

charts.title: What the tail and the spectral slope add to predicting arousal on clips the model had not seen.
charts.takeaway: Adding the two measures raised held-out explained variance by 0.110 (0.034 to 0.182), on top of 0.160 from loudness, genre and year. Shuffled measures added −0.001 on average.
charts.units: gain in held-out explained variance (R2): the share of the spread in arousal ratings on test clips that the model accounts for, with the two measures minus without; higher is a larger gain
charts.n: model fitted on 1,242 clips, scored on 502 held-out clips by 270 artists; 1,000 shuffles
charts.interval: 95% bootstrap interval over artists for the real measures; 5th to 95th percentile of the shuffles for the control
charts.baseline: Tail and slope rows shuffled within the training set and within the test set, and the whole fit repeated 1,000 times (95th percentile +0.003, p 0.0010)
charts.threshold: Gain above 0, interval above 0, and above the shuffle's 95th percentile

axis.label: gain in held-out explained variance (higher is a larger gain)

charts.title: The same link inside each genre (post hoc, run after the verdicts).
charts.takeaway: Inside every one of 11 genres the calm index goes with lower rated arousal, from −0.25 in hip-hop to −0.62 in international music.
charts.units: partial correlation of the calm index with rated arousal inside one genre, loudness and year held fixed; further below 0 is a stronger link
charts.n: 1,743 clips in 11 genres, from 87 to 216 clips each; all clips, training and test together
charts.no_interval: The post hoc file gives one value for each genre, with no interval. Genres with about 100 clips are the least certain.
charts.baseline: The same correlation on all clips with genre held fixed, −0.414

axis.label: partial correlation inside the genre (below 0: calmer sound, lower arousal)

charts.title: How well each sound measure recovers values planted in synthetic music.
charts.takeaway: The tail recovered the planted decay with an error ratio of 0.12 and the spectral slope recovered the planted tilt with 0.21, both under the bar of 0.5. Reverb size scored 0.81 and the constant estimator 1.00. Lower is better.
charts.units: error ratio: a measure's median error against the planted value, divided by its median error against shuffled planted values. 0 is exact recovery, 1 is no better than shuffled targets
charts.n: 40 synthetic clips of 30 seconds with planted room decay, note decay, attack, tempo and tilt; attack time used 32 after 8 dropped
charts.no_interval: The instrument file gives one error ratio for each measure, with no interval.
charts.baseline: The same measure scored against shuffled planted values (ratio 1). A constant estimator runs as a false-success check and has to fail
charts.threshold: Strong: error ratio of 0.5 or less, and median error below the 5th percentile of the shuffled-target errors
charts.planted: Planted values recovered by the two measures the verdicts use: tail (ratio 0.12, rank correlation +0.95) and slope (0.21, +0.99). The constant estimator failed at 1.00
